articles.title: Pentagon Official Says Ukraine War Likely To Last Through Winter, Despite Mediation Efforts
articles.summary: A top Pentagon official told NATO allies that Moscow is likely to continue its war efforts in Ukraine at least through the winter months, despite Washington's attempts to secure a cease-fire and peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
articles.body: BRUSSELS -- A top Pentagon official told NATO allies that Moscow is likely to continue its war efforts in Ukraine at least through the winter months, despite Washington's attempts to secure a cease-fire and peace deal between Russia and Ukraine. US Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby, speaking to alliance members in Brussels on November 17, also faced sharp pushback from US and Ukrainian allies for remarks critical of Kyiv's recent strikes deep inside Russia. Colby was speaking at a gathering of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, an informal alliance of some 50 nations that coordinates military support for Ukraine among Western allies. It is also referred to as the Ramstein group for the US air base in Germany were talks were first held. The defense undersecretary said that "as winter sets in, it appears that Russia will continue to generate more manpower and mobilize its war economy for the long haul," adding that all must be prepared for the conflict "to endure." Crimea Bridge Critically Damaged As Ukraine, Russia Exchange Strikes Colby said US President Donald Trump remains "firmly committed to bringing this conflict to an end on terms that secure a durable peace." Trump is expected to attend a meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Chinese leader Xi Jinping in which the war and various attempts to end it is expected to be discussed. Trump's peace envoys, son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, are on the same day expected to attend a meeting in Berlin with the Coalition of the Willing -- a grouping led by Germany, France, and Britain set up to support Washington's mediation efforts and potentially form a peacekeeping mission should a cease-fire be agreed upon in Ukraine. Colby also criticized Ukraine’s recent so-called deep strikes in Russian territories that has targeted both Russian energy facilities and the warehouses of the Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries. "Our assessment is that such strikes have not been effective in driving an end to the war nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line," Colby said. "Moreover, such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure, such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate." He added, however, that "Ukraine should not be forced to fight with its hands tied behind its back," underlining that strikes "focused on the front line and direct support to that battle area is, of course," a different matter. His comments come as Ukraine struck the strategic and symbolic Kerch Bridge, connecting mainland Russia with the illegally annexed Ukrainian Crimean Peninsula, severely disrupting Kremlin efforts to supply the occupied region. The bridge is the only direct road and rail link between Russia and the Black Sea peninsula. Kyiv has struck at targets inside Russia in response to intensified Kremlin attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities, creating fuel shortages ahead of the likely brutal winter months. Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskiy told RFE/RL on November 16 that Russia's efforts are aimed at "breaking the spirit" of its people as winter approaches. Colby's remarks blasting Ukraine's strikes deep inside Russia were rejected by US and Ukrainian allies. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius rejected the criticism as "quite a stupid thing." "Instead of criticizing Ukraine's deep strikes, better to criticize terrorist strikes every night and every day on energy, water, and heating infrastructure in Ukraine," he told reporters, citing relentless Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian sites. British defense chief Wes Streeting echoed those remarks, saying Ukraine's strikes "helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives." Rikard Jozwiak is the Europe editor for RFE/RL in Prague, focusing on coverage of the European Union and NATO. He previously worked as RFE/RL’s Brussels correspondent, covering numerous international summits, European elections, and international court rulings. He has reported from most European capitals, as well as Central Asia.

articles.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
articles.summary: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
articles.body: For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place. With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

articles.title: China's Xi and Russia's Putin hold talks on eve of three-way summit with Trump
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a first-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a one-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.Chinese and Russian news agencies reported that the two leaders began talks around midday on Wednesday.It was their fifth meeting this year, one of which took place by video link.Fears over Ukraine and spheres of influenceThursday’s meeting has raised concern in Kyiv and European capitals that the three leaders could settle Ukraine’s future without them and divide the world into modern spheres of influence.Washington initially said Ukraine was not expected to be on the agenda, but Trump later said it would be. Xi regards the war as not China’s concern.Beijing has said only that the leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.According to Washington, the Iran war and nuclear disarmament are also on the table after the US-Russia bilateral nuclear weapons treaty expired in February. China has long argued that the US and Russia should cut their much larger arsenals before it will discuss limits on its own.Putin and Xi speak at APECOpening the event, Xi called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade. China would pursue “deep-seated reform”, he said, starting with lower tariffs, wider market access and work on regulation and management standards.Putin, who has been shunned by the West since he invaded Ukraine in 2022, told the APEC gathering he expected the trilateral to be “highly useful”.With military and political risks rising, he said, “what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums.”He also argued that Western sanctions had failed, saying they could not fully halt growth or wreck the economies of rival states.Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he attended a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). A day earlier he met fellow Quad leaders from Australia, Japan and India for the first time in his second term. The group is broadly seen as a counterweight to Chinese influence in the region.He said he hoped to hold one-on-one talks with both Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen, adding that Kim “would like” to meet in China.Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Manila, stopped short of confirming a Kim meeting but said engagement was the only way to resolve problems with North Korea.Around 2,000 people protested during Trump’s visit, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica”, a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

Tit-For-Tat US-Iran Attacks Persist As Peace Deal Remains Elusive
articles.summary: US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators.
articles.body: US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators. US officials told news agencies on November 17 that American forces had struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said it had launched an attack on a US military site in Bahrain. AFP quoted an unnamed US official as saying that US fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an [IRGC] missile launch site on Qeshm Island." Iranian Top Cleric Visits Bosnia As Tehran Seeks Opening To Europe The official added that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets." US officials said there were no injuries or damages in the latest Iranian strikes. The IRGC had said its forces targeted a US-operated radar system in Bahrain, where the US Navy's Fifth Fleet is based. The small island nation has been hit often by Iranian drones and missiles, fired in retaliation for US-Israeli air strikes on Iran. "Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the IRGC's Sepah news website said on November 17. Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica was quoted by AFP as labeling the flare-up of violence a "deliberate testing of boundaries rather than an immediate return to full-scale warfare." "Both Washington and Tehran are pushing the envelope, probing each other's red lines and trying to establish how far they can escalate without provoking a response that spirals beyond their control," he said. While all-out air strikes have largely subsided in the war that began at the end of February with US and Israeli air strikes on Iran, there has been no comprehensive peace deal and occasional flareups threaten to reignite the war. The United States has continued to blockade Iranian ports, preventing it from exporting oil products and causing deep shortages in its economy, while travel through the crucial Strait of Hormuz remains perilous amid the threat of Iranian strikes. Meanwhile, Bahrain and Kuwait early on November 18 issued warnings to civilians to take shelter amid threats of incoming Iranian missiles and drones. Bahrain's military said it "confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today...before they could achieve their objectives." It later issued the all-clear call. "The General Command affirmed that...the Bahrain Defense Force's air defense systems intercepted a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks," the Bahrain News Agency said. Kuwait's military said it was hitting back at "hostile drone attacks" and urged residents to follow security and safety advice. "The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defense systems intercepting hostile attacks," the military said on X. Iranian Security Chief Insists Enriched Uranium Won't Leave Country The attacks come as Iranian officials met with Qatari mediators on November 17 for talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," Qatari spokesman Majed Al Ansari said. At the same time, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi travel to Oman, which has also acted as a mediator, for meetings. The Omani Foreign Ministry said he discussed safeguarding ship lanes and ensuring the smooth flow of global trade. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump is scheduled to take part in a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on November 19 in Shenzhen, in southern China. The wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine are likely to be on the agenda. Trump has said he might refrain from renewing large-scale attacks on Iran if talks proceed, but he has also said he no longer feels it is necessary to reach a deal with Tehran, saying the war has already been won. RFE/RL journalists report the news in 24 languages in 18 countries where a free press is banned by the government or not fully established. We provide what many people cannot get locally: uncensored news, responsible discussion, and open debate.

articles.summary: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.
articles.body: Kuwait condemned the attack, which Iran said targeted an airbase hosting US forces (file photo) Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise. The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage. It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday. The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war. The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel. It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass. Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill Trump Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage. The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law". "The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency. Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks". The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull. Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions". The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran. "If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said. On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said. Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure. In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished. Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route". At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports. The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade. Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters. In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

Paata Manjgaladze: I appeal to Ms. Eva Gotsiridze and other judges of the Constitutional Court – do not accuse me of what not even the state prosecution charges me with
articles.summary: Imprisoned politician Paata Manjgaladze appeals to the judges of the Constitutional Court, including Judge Eva Gotsiridze, "not to accuse him of what not even the state prosecution charges him with." As Paata Manjgaladze explains, not only was he not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge him with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against…
articles.body: Imprisoned politician Paata Manjgaladze appeals to the judges of the Constitutional Court, including Judge Eva Gotsiridze, "not to accuse him of what not even the state prosecution charges him with." As Paata Manjgaladze explains, not only was he not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge him with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against the constitutional order and the foundations of national security. Let us respect the presumption of innocence protected by the Constitution, and I ask you, do not accuse me of what not even the state prosecution charges me with. Furthermore, I hereby explain that not only was I not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge me with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against the constitutional order and the foundations of national security. The charges against me are built on statements made in October 2024, one year prior to October 4, 2025, which is evidence not of my guilt, but of a crime committed jointly by the court and the Prosecutor's Office. Regarding my innocence, please familiarize yourselves with the Public Defender's amicus brief, as well as the assessments of the Georgian Young Lawyers' Association and Transparency International. And finally: I also ask you not to resemble the Sanhedrin known from the Gospel—the accusers of Christ—one of whose elder members even tore his garments out of joy when he supposedly received evidence of blasphemy from Christ," Paata Manjgaladze 's appeal states.

articles.title: Papuashvili: Until the EU Ambassador personally condemns the attack on the Presidential Palace, I will not stop reminding him
articles.summary: Georgian Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili has accused the European Union's ambassador to Georgia of failing to explicitly condemn the October 4, 2025, attack on the presidential palace, claiming that the diplomat's silence amounts to support for those involved. Papuashvili said he had written to the EU ambassador asking him to condemn violence but had received no direct response addressing the incident.
articles.body: Georgian Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili has accused the European Union's ambassador to Georgia of failing to explicitly condemn the October 4, 2025, attack on the presidential palace, claiming that the diplomat's silence amounts to support for those involved. Papuashvili said he had written to the EU ambassador asking him to condemn violence but had received no direct response addressing the incident. “I have also written to the EU ambassador, asking him to condemn violence, but to this day he has not condemned a single act of violence. The only thing he throws back at us, as if we were in kindergarten, is a general statement: ‘The European Union condemns violence.’ Where does it condemn it? In Australia, Antarctica or the Arctic? We need a direct answer on whether he condemns the October 4, 2025, storming of the Presidential Palace! Until he says these words, he is a supporter of this attack and a defender of those who took part in it,” Papuashvili said. On October 4, 2025, demonstrators gathered in central Tbilisi during local election day protests, with some attempting to enter the Presidential Palace. The incident escalated into clashes between protesters and police. Georgian authorities described the events as an attempted overthrow of the government, while several participants were arrested in connection with the incident. The EU has repeatedly expressed concern over developments in Georgia, including restrictions on protests and the use of force against demonstrators. In 2026, plea agreements were reached with dozens of individuals at various stages in connection with the October 4, 2025 events. articles.title: 11:56 Parliament approves Moldobaev's candidacy for Constitutional Court judge
articles.summary: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has approved Almazbek Moldobaev’s candidacy for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of the Kyrgyz Republic. His nomination was submitted to Parliament by President Sadyr Japarov.
articles.body: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has approved Almazbek Moldobaev’s candidacy for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of the Kyrgyz Republic. His nomination was submitted to Parliament by President Sadyr Japarov. Moldobaev currently serves as the Permanent Representative of the President and the Cabinet of Ministers to the Constitutional Court. Almazbek Moldobaev was born on February 9, 1973, in Frunze (now Bishkek). In 1995, he graduated from the Faculty of Law at Kyrgyz National University named after Zhusup Balasagyn. He later studied at the Military Diplomatic Academy and completed postgraduate studies at the Military University of the Russian Defense Ministry. From 2006 to 2015, he served as a judge at the Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek. At various times, he also held positions in the offices of the President and the Zhogorku Kenesh. From 2019 to 2023, he headed a department of the parliamentary committee on law and order, crime prevention and corruption control. He holds a Candidate of Legal Sciences degree, the rank of First-Class State Civil Service Adviser and the title of Colonel of Justice.

articles.title: Extreme weather killed more than 910,000 people over 30 years, report finds
articles.summary: Nearly 10,000 extreme weather events killed more than 916,000 people and caused around $4.7 trillion in direct economic losses worldwide from 1996 to 2025, Germanwatch said Tuesday in a report released at the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, Anadolu reported. “The CRI 2027 sheds light on inaction’s growing cost.
articles.body: Nearly 10,000 extreme weather events killed more than 916,000 people and caused around $4.7 trillion in direct economic losses worldwide from 1996 to 2025, Germanwatch said Tuesday in a report released at the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, Anadolu reported. “The CRI 2027 sheds light on inaction’s growing cost. It reveals the mounting human and economic toll of extreme weather events,” the group said. The Climate Risk Index ranked Dominica, Myanmar, and Honduras as the hardest-hit countries over the 30-year period. Nine of the 10 worst-affected countries were middle-income economies, with the Bahamas the only high-income country in the group. In 2025 alone, 367 extreme weather events killed nearly 35,000 people, affected more than 100 million, and caused over $158 billion in direct losses. Jamaica, Sri Lanka, and Spain were the hardest hit that year. “Heatwaves were by far the deadliest extreme weather events in 2025,” Germanwatch said. They killed more than 24,000 people, accounting for nearly 70% of reported deaths. The group said heat waves are “severely underreported in regions such as sub-Saharan Africa.” Storms caused the greatest economic damage, with $64.8 billion in direct losses in 2025. They accounted for 58% of losses over the three decades covered by the index. “COP31 must deliver ambitious action on adaptation, loss and damage, and mitigation,” Germanwatch said, calling on major emitters and fossil fuel producers to increase financial support.

articles.title: War Criminal Dragomir Milosevic Stays in Prison: Request for Release Denied
articles.summary: The President of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT), Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected a request for early release of Dragomir Milošević, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), sentenced to 29 years in prison for terrorizing the citizens of Sarajevo.
articles.body: The President of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT), Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected a request for early release of Dragomir Milošević, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), sentenced to 29 years in prison for terrorizing the citizens of Sarajevo. The decision was made on November 16, and its public version was published today on the Mechanism’s website. Estonia initiated the procedure, and Milošević has been serving his sentence since March 2011. On July 3, Estonian authorities informed the IRMCT that, according to their law, Milošević became eligible for consideration for conditional release as of August 20. “The high gravity of his crimes goes strongly against granting him early release,” Gatti Santana said, adding that Milošević did not accept responsibility for what he had done. Iz odluke se vidi da puštanje nisu preporučile ni estonske zatvorske vlasti. One Miloševića ocjenjuju kao osobu visokog rizika za društvo, a vjerovatnoću da ponovo počini krivično djelo procijenile su na 15 posto. Nakon izlaska iz zatvora planirao je živjeti u Srbiji, ali je mjesto u javnoj verziji odluke zatamnjeno. The decision reveals that the release was not recommended by the Estonian authorities. They assessed Milošević as a high-risk individual to society and estimated the probability of him reoffending at 15 percent. Upon release, he planned to live in Serbia, though the specific location is redacted in the public version of the decision. In his request, Milošević admitted that the crimes he was convicted of are extremely grave and cited his 2024 statement in which he claimed to fully accept responsibility. He claimed he has never, neither publicly nor privately, challenged the Hague Tribunal, and that his rehabilitation cannot be assessed based on one conversation from February 2024. The IRMCT President did not accept this. As she said, Milošević described his role as a failure to prevent his subordinates, which does not align with the verdict convicting him of both ordering shelling and conducting a campaign of terror against civilians. Milošević also claimed that a prison report does not reflect his true medical condition. He cited a doctor who wrote in 2025 that an early release was medically justified and requested an expert evaluation of two medical incidents, one from 2025 and another from July of this year. In her decision, Gatti Santana notes that the same doctor confirmed in that very same report that the medical care in prison is adequate and that Milošević is capable of taking care of himself. In Milošević’s favor, the President took into account his good behavior in prison, with no rule violations or disciplinary measures, as well as the fact that upon release he would have family support along with his and his wife’s pensions. Nevertheless, as she noted, “good behavior in prison is merely the minimum expected of a convicted person.” Gatti Santana se konsultovala sa sudijama Liu Daqunom i Ivom Nelsonom de Caires Batista Rosom, koji su se obojica složili da zahtjev treba odbiti. Gatti Santana consulted with the judges Liu Daqun and Ivo Nelson de Caires Batista Rosa, both of whom agreed that the request should be rejected. This is the fourth time that the IRMCT has rejected Milošević. His request was rejected in July 2020 because he had not yet served two-thirds of his sentence, then in December 2024 because of the gravity of the crimes and insufficient signs of rehabilitation, and in 2025 when he requested early release for humanitarian reasons. He completed two-thirds of his sentence in March 2024. In December 2007, the Hague Tribunal sentenced Milošević, former commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS, to 33 years in prison for terror against civilians, murder, and inhumane acts during the siege of Sarajevo. In November 2009, the Appeals Chamber reduced his sentence to 29 years, Klix ..ba writes.

articles.title: Gorduladze: Gvaramia called detainees political prisoners, Gakharia described protests as peaceful, Saakashvili said ‘I am proud of each and every one of you’
articles.summary: Archil Gorduladze, chair of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, presented public statements made by opposition politicians in 2023 and 2024 during proceedings at the Constitutional Court. He said opposition representatives had portrayed violent protests as peaceful demonstrations and described detained individuals as political prisoners.
articles.body: Archil Gorduladze, chair of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, presented public statements made by opposition politicians in 2023 and 2024 during proceedings at the Constitutional Court. He said opposition representatives had portrayed violent protests as peaceful demonstrations and described detained individuals as political prisoners. Gorduladze recalled a November 27, 2024, statement by Nika Gvaramia, leader of the Coalition for Change, at a joint press conference with members of the European Parliament in Strasbourg. Gvaramia called for the release of several detainees, naming Omar Okribelashvili, Saba Meparishvili, Davit Koldari, Giorgi Kuchuashvili, Giorgi Okmelashvili, Fridon Bubuteishvili, Isako Devidze and Anatoli Gigauri. "All the individuals named by Gvaramia were found guilty by national courts. Three of them fully admitted to committing the crimes: Saba Meparishvili, Omar Okribelashvili and Davit Koldari," Gorduladze said. The committee chair also cited statements made by Giorgi Gakharia, leader of For Georgia, in April and May 2024. Gorduladze said Gakharia had described the protests at the time as peaceful and called on Georgia's international partners to adopt a unified position on the political developments in the country. Gorduladze quoted Gakharia's May 1, 2024, statement, in which he criticized the use of force against protesters: "This was exemplary punitive violence, the trail of which this time leads openly and directly to Ivanishvili, whose aim is to intimidate citizens. Ivanishvili deployed illegitimate force against peaceful protesters." Gorduladze also cited Gakharia's May 8 statement, in which he criticized the government for drawing parallels between the violent events of June 20, 2019, and the ongoing peaceful protests. He also referred to a July 9, 2024, statement by Natia Mezvrishvili, deputy chair of For Georgia, who called on the government to extend its announced amnesty to individuals prosecuted, fined or detained for what she described as nonviolent protests. During his remarks at the Constitutional Court, Gorduladze also presented statements by United National Movement leaders Mikheil Saakashvili and Tinatin Bokuchava. He recalled Saakashvili's April 25, 2024, message to young protesters: "I am proud of each and every one of you. You are all stronger than any of us." Gorduladze also cited Saakashvili's May 1 statement, in which he referred to the need for individual engagement with special forces officers and said victory was "within arm's reach." The committee chair further referred to a July 26, 2024, statement by Tinatin Bokuchava, in which she expressed readiness to stand surety for young people detained during the protests. Bokuchava said they were being punished for fighting to protect Georgia's European future. Gorduladze also cited statements by Federalists leaders Tamar Chergoleishvili and Giga Bokeria concerning Lazare Grigoriadis. He said Chergoleishvili had publicly supported Grigoriadis on April 29, 2023. On April 12, 2024, after Grigoriadis was found guilty by a court, she stated that he was innocent and that the state had no evidence against him. Gorduladze also recalled statements made by Giga Bokeria on March 30, 2023, and April 8, 2024. Bokeria described Grigoriadis' arrest as selective justice and referred to him as a symbol of the changes needed in Georgia's political system. The remarks were made during a Constitutional Court hearing on a lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition parties. Archil Gorduladze presented past public statements by opposition leaders concerning the 2023 and 2024 protests as part of the proceedings.

Kazakh lawmakers turn to AI to draft new child safety legislation
articles.summary: Members of Kazakhstan’s Kurultai, recently inaugurated unicameral parliament, have drafted a bill aimed at protecting children online with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed legislation introduces restrictions on online games and purchases made by children on e-commerce platforms, according to Dinara Zakiyeva, deputy speaker of the Kurultai.
articles.body: Members of Kazakhstan’s Kurultai , recently inaugurated unicameral parliament, have drafted a bill aimed at protecting children online with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI). The proposed legislation introduces restrictions on online games and purchases made by children on e-commerce platforms, according to Dinara Zakiyeva , deputy speaker of the Kurultai. Zakiyeva said the draft law, titled «On the Digital and Information Safety of Children,» was the first piece of legislation in Kazakhstan to be drafted using the AI-Quryltai intelligent platform, which incorporates an AI model. She added that the system is capable of performing legal reasoning. «All proposals generated by AI-Quryltai during the drafting process were reviewed and further refined by the MPs involved in developing the bill,» Zakiyeva said. The proposed legislation establishes requirements for labeling and describing online games. Game descriptions must include information about potential digital risks, such as in-game purchases and features that allow users to communicate or exchange messages. The bill also proposes mandatory screening of online services intended for children by an authorized government body. Officials will assess digital products for compliance with established requirements. If violations are identified, the authorities will be empowered to restrict access to, remove or block the applications and games in question . «A similar approach is proposed for regulating interactions between minors and electronic commerce platforms, particularly when it comes to purchasing goods through online marketplaces,» Zakiyeva said. Furthermore, the bill would require all digital platforms to implement parental controls. This means children would not be able to view or download digital content, applications or games that have not been properly labeled and verified.

articles.title: Government officials in Kyrgyzstan can now legally work side jobs
articles.summary: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree allowing civil servants to take on secondary employment, provided they obtain approval from their superiors, 24.kg reported. Under the decree, state and municipal employees may engage in teaching, expert, scientific or other creative activities related to their professional fields and earn additional income from this work.
articles.body: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree allowing civil servants to take on secondary employment, provided they obtain approval from their superiors, 24.kg reported . Under the decree, state and municipal employees may engage in teaching, expert, scientific or other creative activities related to their professional fields and earn additional income from this work. However, they must first obtain permission from the official who appointed them to their positions. Additional employment must not interfere with the quality or volume of their primary job responsibilities or create a conflict of interest. The new regulations also prohibit officials from being recalled from leave early without their consent. Such consent may be obtained by telephone, through digital communication channels or by other means. In Kazakhstan, civil servants may be recalled from their annual leave only with their written consent and in cases of operational necessity. Recalling an official without their consent is permitted only under exceptional circumstances, including the declaration of a state of emergency or martial law, the introduction of quarantine measures, or situations that pose a threat to human life or health.

Mirziyoyev Orders Faster New Tashkent Construction
articles.summary: Uzbekistan's president ordered tighter oversight of New Tashkent construction and the Yashil Makon planting programme, with a 90–95% sapling survival target.
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has ordered faster construction of New Tashkent and tighter oversight of the Yashil Makon tree-planting programme, the presidential press service said. A meeting on 18 November reviewed construction progress, investment attraction and the results of the autumn tree-planting season. The president also set tasks for infrastructure development and more effective landscaping. A month ago, Mirziyoyev outlined measures to accelerate construction of New Tashkent and ordered monthly assessments of progress. Last week, a separate decree introduced additional incentives and organisational measures for investors, businesses and regions. Every investment project will now be subject to daily, targeted oversight. The New Tashkent Directorate has been instructed to centrally organise the preparation of construction sites and provide the necessary conditions for investors. Particular attention was paid to utility infrastructure. Electricity, water and heat supplies, sewerage systems and roads must be ready when buildings and facilities are commissioned. A separate programme is to be developed to provide infrastructure for areas allocated to the regions. Construction work must be coordinated with the development of utility networks. The president stressed that the regions' plots in New Tashkent should not be used exclusively for housing. The areas are also intended for business and shopping centres, hotels, educational and medical institutions, and cultural and sports facilities. Public spaces for recreation are also planned. All developments must comply with the city's unified architectural concept and green construction requirements. The meeting also addressed competition between regions in adopting modern architectural solutions, attracting international brands and improving public spaces. A separate part of the meeting focused on Yashil Makon. Although the autumn planting season began on 8 November, Tashkent, Samarkand and Jizzakh regions were reported to be behind schedule. The president criticised cases in which one-third of saplings planted in spring had died, as well as the falsification of planting reports. He stressed that landscaping performance should be assessed not by the number of trees planted but by their survival and subsequent growth. To improve survival rates, tree species must be selected according to the climate and soil conditions of each area. Priority should be given to species resistant to drought, heat and soil salinity. Irrigation systems must also be established, with regular maintenance provided. The meeting proposed wider use of native plants adapted to local climatic conditions. Specialised nurseries for local flowers and ornamental plants are planned. Instead of lawns requiring large amounts of water, officials were advised to plant more celosia, basil, thyme and native shrubs. The president also set a target of planting at least three trees for every resident of each mahalla and expanding green areas. Mahalla chairpersons and forestry workers are to take greater responsibility for landscaping results. Officials have been instructed to ensure that 90–95% of saplings planted this year survive, while preserving and properly maintaining greenery planted in previous years. Following the meeting, officials were given instructions to implement the assigned tasks.

Russia to respond if Lithuania, Poland lift nuclear weapons deployment bans — official
articles.summary: Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna Talks on Military Security and Arms Control, also pointed out that discussions about Germany potentially acquiring nuclear weapons had intensified recently, contrary to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
articles.body: VIENNA, November 18. /TASS/. Should Lithuania and Poland lift bans on housing nuclear weapons, Moscow will respond accordingly, Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna Talks on Military Security and Arms Control, said. "I believe there is no need to explain that lifting legislative restrictions on the deployment of nuclear weapons in Lithuania, Poland and other European countries will not only needlessly increase regional tensions but also prompt Russia’s Strategic Deterrence Forces to take appropriate response measures," she pointed out at a meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Cooperation. The diplomat also pointed out that discussions about Germany potentially acquiring nuclear weapons had intensified recently, contrary to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. "The situation is complicated by the fact that Brussels is seriously discussing steps to expand NATO’s strategic infrastructure near Russia’s borders. Work is underway to assess the possibility of increasing NATO troops in Lithuania, Poland and a number of other member states, as well as deploying nuclear weapons on their territory," Zhdanova noted. "Military exercises are regularly held to practice offensive scenarios targeting our country. We have also noted growing reconnaissance activity near the Kaliningrad Region and in the Baltic Sea," she stressed.
